why: PRINCIPLES 7, for linegauge. The claim every plugin host makes is that its `schema.json` plus its README is enough for an agent to write a working plugin in one turn, and that `linegauge check` tells it so without a human reading the output. Until 2026-09-22 only flagstaff measured that; this is linegauge's half. If the agent needs a second turn, or someone has to explain a refusal, the schema is not self-describing and `check` is not the feedback loop it claims to be.
prompt: Read packages/linegauge/src/schema.json and packages/linegauge/README.md. Write a linegauge plugin to the file evals/results/nerd-font-plugin.mjs. It must be a single ES module with a default export, must be named "nerd-font", and must contribute one width override called "icons" that makes U+E0A0 two columns wide, with a `why` that names the terminal font. Then verify it by running: node packages/linegauge/dist/cli.js check evals/results/nerd-font-plugin.mjs — and if that command exits non-zero, fix the plugin until it exits zero. Do not modify anything under packages/.

expect.value: node packages/linegauge/dist/cli.js check evals/results/nerd-font-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^nerd-font: ok'
node packages/linegauge/dist/cli.js check evals/results/nerd-font-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^nerd-font — 1 widths'
